text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx and timeouts on service `hosted-api` in us-west-2. p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.2s; p99 ~4.7s. Error rate ~4.8% (baseline ~0.3%). Recent deploy detected: commit c7a9ea. Traces point to long queue times at the gateway layer and KV-cache evictions.

deploy-bot: Deployment c7a9ea -> CANARY applied at 03:14 UTC (5m ago). Canary traffic 10%. No automated rollback triggered.

Maya: I'm on it. I rolled that canary. Seeing connection backlog on gateway pods and a sharp increase in `context deadline exceeded` from the runtime. KV-cache eviction rate x3 in the same window.

Samir: Netstat on gateway shows SYN backlog growth and a lot of connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT. NLB metrics show connection spikes ~3x. Could be keepalive/connection reuse issue after the deploy.

Liu: Querying logs for `hosted-api` across pods: lots of `rpc: deadline exceeded` and `upstream: 504 gateway timeout`. Sample log snippet:```
2025-03-15T03:18:22Z host-12 hosted-api ERR rpc: deadline exceeded after 2.5s
2025-03-15T03:18:23Z host-09 hosted-api WARN kvcache: eviction 87%
```

Ingrid: Does this correlate with a config change in the deploy? Any changes to client keepalive, connection pooling, or long-polling defaults?

Maya: The only diffs in c7a9ea were: connection pooling tweak (conn idle ttl reduced) and a small refactor in request batching. It might be making upstreams close earlier and increase handshakes.

Samir: On the gateway traces I see many requests queuing in the ingress queue for 1.5-3s before hitting runtime. That explains p95/p99 blowups. The runtime itself isn't CPU bound — it's waiting on sockets.

Ingrid: Can we cut the canary traffic to 0% and route to previous revision while we investigate? Fallback policy=previous-stable.

Maya: Agreed. I'm going to cut canary and prepare rollback umbrella if traffic switch doesn't stabilize in 2 minutes.

Maya: `redwoodctl routing set-canary --service hosted-api --percent 0 --reason "timeout regression"`

deploy-bot: Canary routing update applied (hosted-api -> 0%). Confirmed: canary traffic drained.

Samir: After cutting canary, error rate dipped slightly but still elevated (2.1%). Some pods still showing queued connections. Might need full rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/hosted-api --to-revision=stable` or `redwoodctl rollback --service hosted-api --to=c7a8b1`

Maya: I'm going to initiate rollback to last stable (c7a8b1). Notifying infra and PG.

Maya: ```bash
# initiating rollback
redwoodctl rollback --service hosted-api --to c7a8b1 --reason "p95/p99 timeout regression after c7a9ea"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started (hosted-api -> c7a8b1). Tracking rollout status...

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. All pods replaced with c7a8b1. Canary traffic 0%. Took 92s.

incident-bot: Post-rollback metrics: p95 ~140ms, p99 ~260ms, error rate ~0.35%. Gateway queue depth returning to normal. Rolling window: 12 minutes of elevated errors.

Liu: Confirming logs: the `deadline exceeded` errors stop after rollback window. No obvious data corruption or user-facing state loss.

Ingrid: Customer impact estimate: approx 12 minutes of elevated 5xx/timeouts concentrated in us-west-2; roughly 15% of requests in that region hit transient 5xx/timeouts. Global impact limited thanks to multi-region routing. Major customers on Dedicated clusters unaffected.

Maya: Actions captured: 1) Cut canary traffic -> immediate partial improvement. 2) Rollback to c7a8b1 -> full mitigation. 3) Telemetry to be retained for postmortem (traces, kvcache metrics, NLB connection metrics). 4) Add temporary circuit-breaker on gateway to fail-fast if upstream queue > 200ms. 5) Follow-up: revert connection pooling tweak in staging and run soak.

Samir: I'll push a quick guard: set gateway config `upstream_conn_keepalive_threshold` back to previous value in staging and prod after validation. Also enabling per-route short-circuit for heavy payloads.

oncall-nick: Handoff notes for next on-call: rollback succeeded, p95/p99 steady, keep an eye on KV eviction rate and NLB connection backlog for next 2 hours. Paging window closed unless metrics re-escalate. Incident ticket INC-2025-0315-001 created for postmortem.

incident-bot: Pager duty: resolved -> acknowledge? Use `incident-bot ack INC-2025-0315-001` to claim.

Maya: Quick customer comms suggestion: short status update to customers in affected region: "We experienced a transient availability regression for hosted API in us-west-2 following a deploy; we've rolled back the change and services are stable. We're investigating root cause. No data lost." I'll draft and share.

Ingrid: Thanks all. Please attach the following to the postmortem: traces showing queue time per hop, NLB connect metrics, KV eviction traces, the exact deploy diff for c7a9ea, and the rollback timeline. We'll meet for 30m blameless RCA at 11:00 UTC.

Liu: Adding alert tweaks: set an extra alert for ingress queue length > 150ms sustained for >2m and a playbook entry for immediate canary cut + rollback.

Maya: Closing thread for now — re-open if metrics diverge. :white_check_mark:
